spot.html_text: But Frege noticed (1892a) that this account of truth can’t be all there is to the meaning of identity statements. The statement ‘ ⟦M⟧ ’ has a cognitive significance (or meaning) that must be different from the cognitive significance of ‘ ⟦M⟧ ’. We can learn that ‘Mark Twain = Mark Twain’ is true simply by inspecting it; but we can’t learn the truth of ‘Mark Twain = Samuel Clemens’ simply by inspecting it — you have to examine the world to see whether the two persons are the same.
